articles.title: SJAA EPHEMERIS
articles.summary: This document is the masthead for the January 1996 edition (Volume 7, Number 1) of the "SJAA EPHEMERIS." It identifies the publication as the official bulletin of the San Jose Astronomical Association, indicating its introductory nature for that month's content.

articles.title: Eye on the Ephemerides
articles.summary: This article from "Eye on the Ephemerides" provides updates and a detailed calendar of events for an astronomy club, likely SJAA. It outlines upcoming talks on topics such as CCD techniques and a solar eclipse, details the annual Board of Directors elections and budget meeting, and announces the annual Swap Meet. The document also lists a comprehensive schedule of general meetings, star parties, and astronomy classes for January and February.

articles.title: Gregory Award Presented!
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) presented its A.B. Gregory Award to member Bob Ashford, recognizing his outstanding dedication to astronomy education and outreach, including teaching at schools and leading star parties. The award honors Dr. A.B. Gregory, a former SJAA president and amateur astronomer known for inspiring many through his observational astronomy classes.

articles.title: Observing Report
articles.summary: On Saturday, November 18, members of the SJAA and friends gathered at Fremont Peak for an observing session. Despite initially promising conditions that allowed for targeting Herschel objects in Cetus and Pisces, heavy dew quickly cut the viewing short. The group then spent time socializing and enjoyed a good show from the active Leonids meteor shower before departing.

articles.title: Thank You
articles.summary: Jim Van Nuland extends heartfelt thanks to all volunteers who participate in school and Houge Park public star parties, acknowledging their crucial role in providing views of the night sky to students, parents, teachers, and passers-by. He emphasizes that their efforts are deeply appreciated, and an editor's note encourages more individuals to volunteer for these San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) programs.

articles.title: January's General Meeting Talk
articles.summary: Shiloh Unruh, historian at Lick Observatory, will be speaking at the January 6, 1996, General Meeting. He will discuss his newly completed murder mystery book, which features the daughter of James Lick's administrator as the victim and involves several well-known astronomers. Attendees are encouraged to learn the unsolved mystery's outcome from this outstanding speaker.

articles.title: Eclipse over India
articles.summary: Ernie Piini, a member of the San Jose Astronomical Association, will present a color slide show on March 2 about his challenging 42-second Total Solar Eclipse experience over northern India on October 24, 1995. His talk will also cover his travels through India, including sights like the Taj Mahal, and discussions on ancient observatories and future eclipses.

articles.title: Snatching Victory from the Jaws of Clouds
articles.summary: An astronomy outreach event at Dartmouth school, initially threatened by heavy cloud cover, unexpectedly cleared up after an alternative slide show was presented. Despite the initial cloudy conditions, the sky eventually opened, allowing students and parents to observe celestial objects like Saturn, Altair, and various clusters through telescopes. The event was a success, demonstrating the unpredictable nature of sky conditions and the benefit of taking a chance on a cloudy evening.

articles.title: Useful Magnification Limits
articles.summary: Jay Freeman's article details the useful magnification limits for telescopes, explaining that minimum magnification is determined by the observer's eye pupil and telescope aperture to match the exit pupil. Maximum magnification varies significantly based on atmospheric steadiness, optical quality, and observer visual acuity. The author also provides practical advice for beginners on selecting eyepieces, suggesting starting with a low-power eyepiece for deep-sky objects and finding, followed by a medium-high power option.

articles.title: Happy Birthday SJAA, What a Wonderful Meeting We Had
articles.summary: The article recounts a successful San Jose Amateur Astronomers (SJAA) birthday meeting, organized by Bob Madden, which brought together original members like Richard Barrett and John Delaney. John Delaney and Jim Van Nuland shared historical accounts of the club's founding in 1954 and early activities, including the construction of a 12.5-inch telescope. The event fostered reconnections among long-time members, celebrated the club's history with cake, and served as a heartwarming gathering for the astronomy community.

articles.title: Club Finances
articles.summary: This report details the club's financial status as of December 8, indicating that the club is financially sound with year-to-date income exceeding expenses. It outlines various fund balances, discusses Ephemeris publication costs, the Gregory award, and addresses the reimbursement for telescope maintenance and building supplies. The article also confirms the finalized annual fee for AL insurance, which is within the budgeted amount.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: This document, the "Periodical Publication Statement," announces that "The SJAA Ephemeris," the newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly. It clarifies that the publication is released 12 times a year, from January through December, and includes the association's address.

articles.title: Jaws, continued from page 3
articles.summary: The article describes a successful event, overcoming initial risks through persistence. The following night, an event at Buchser school also proved perfect, with clear skies, engaged participants, and good food.

articles.title: Public Information Office
articles.summary: This document provides contact information for the Public Information Office of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), an entity of the California Institute of Technology and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). It lists the Pasadena address and phone number for inquiries.

articles.title: GALILEO MISSION STATUS
articles.summary: The Galileo spacecraft successfully achieved orbit around Jupiter in December 1995, with precise targeting leading to the cancellation of planned maneuvers and an earlier Ganymede flyby. The mission commenced transmitting crucial data from its atmospheric probe, which completed a 57-minute plunge into Jupiter's atmosphere, marking the first direct measurements of an outer planet's atmosphere. While initial data analysis began for a December 19 press briefing (later postponed), data transmission was temporarily halted due to solar conjunction.

articles.title: COMET COMMENTS, 12-06-1995
articles.summary: Don Machholz's "Comet Comments" from December 1995 reports on Comet 45P/Honda-Mrkos-Pajdusakova brightening and approaching Earth in early 1996. The article also details Comet Hale-Bopp's status, noting it is currently behind the sun but will emerge in February 1996 to remain visible through the end of the decade, with the Northern Hemisphere favored from April 1996 to April 1997. Earth will pass close to Hale-Bopp's orbit in January 1996, though no meteor shower is anticipated.

articles.title: EPHEMERIDES
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for four comets: 122P/de Vico, C/1995 Q1 (Bradfield), 73P/Schwassman-Wachmann 3, and 45P/Honda-Mrkos-Pajdusakova. It lists their celestial coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), elongation from the Sun, and predicted magnitude at 00 UT for dates spanning from late December to early February. This data is essential for astronomers to locate and observe these comets.

articles.title: ORBITAL ELEMENTS
articles.summary: This document presents a table of orbital elements for four distinct celestial objects: de Vico, Bradfield, Schwassman-Wachmann 3, and Honda-Mrkos-Pajdusakova. For each object, key parameters such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, and orbital period are detailed. The data, sourced from various MPC and IAU catalogs, provides critical information for tracking these astronomical bodies.

articles.title: Lunar Phase
articles.summary: This document provides a detailed schedule of the major lunar phases for a specific period, including Full Moon (FM), Last Quarter (LQ), New Moon (NM), and First Quarter (FQ). For each phase, it lists the exact time and date in PST, along with the moon's corresponding rise, transit, and set times.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for Mercury, including its distance from Earth and apparent magnitude. It features an ephemeris table detailing rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) for three specific dates (07, 17, 27).

articles.title: Venus
articles.summary: This document provides current astronomical data for Venus, detailing its distance, magnitude, and crucial observational timings. It lists rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension and Declination coordinates, for three specific dates: the 7th, 17th, and 27th.

articles.title: Mars
articles.summary: This document provides current astronomical data for Mars, including its distance from Earth and apparent magnitude. It also features an ephemeris for three specific dates, detailing the planet's rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension and Declination.

articles.title: Jupiter
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for Jupiter, detailing its distance, magnitude, and celestial coordinates (RA and Dec) for various dates. It also includes rise, transit, and set times, likely for observing purposes over a specific period.

articles.title: Saturn
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for the planet Saturn, including its current distance and apparent magnitude. It also lists ephemeris data for three specific dates, detailing rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension and Declination coordinates for observational planning.

articles.title: SOL Star Type G2V Intelligent Life in System ?
articles.summary: The document presents a table of astronomical observation data, including rise, transit, and set times, along with Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) for three specific dates. The title speculatively questions the presence of intelligent life within a G2V star system, which is the stellar classification of our Sun, hinting at a connection to the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

articles.title: Astronomical Twilight
articles.summary: This document presents a concise table detailing the start and end times of astronomical twilight for specific Julian Dates. It provides a quick reference for these crucial periods for astronomical observation over a short span of days.

articles.title: Sidereal Time
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for January 1996, including sidereal time at local midnight, and sunset, twilight, and moonset times for the darkest Saturday night (January 20). It also lists a calendar of events for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) from January to March 1996, featuring general meetings, star parties, and observational astronomy classes, advising members to consult their Ephemeris for updates.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Status
articles.summary: This document outlines the current status of telescopes available for loan, listing various models, their current borrowers, and due dates. It indicates which telescopes are presently available for use and provides contact information for Paul Barton to arrange borrowing, along with a note about an unreachable borrower.

articles.title: ASTRO ADS
articles.summary: ASTRO ADS serves as a free classifieds section for noncommercial advertisers offering astronomy-related products and services. The current listings include a 12.5-inch Star Instruments Ritchy Chretien telescope and a 10.1-inch Odyssey Dobsonian telescope, both for sale. Additionally, there is a 'wanted' ad seeking cabinet-grade plywood for a homemade Dobsonian telescope.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the officers and board of directors of an organization, including their names and contact phone numbers. It also identifies contributors to the 'Ephemeris' publication and its editor, Lew Kurtz. The article concludes with guidelines for members to submit articles for publication in the monthly newsletter, specifying preferred formats and the submission deadline.

articles.title: SAN JOSE ASTRONOMICAL ASSOCIATION MEMBERSHIP
articles.summary: This document is a membership application form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA). It outlines different membership tiers, including options with or without a subscription to Sky and Telescope magazine, and provides instructions for submitting the form and payment to the SJAA treasurer.

articles.title: SJAA HOTLINE
articles.summary: The SJAA Hotline provides 24-hour information through a dedicated phone number. It also references an ephemeris for January 1996, indicating a resource for celestial data likely part of a larger publication or service.
